record.paper_title: A Survey on Physics Informed Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can physics be incorporated in data-driven model learning in a way that generalizes across different tasks and environments in physics-informed reinforcement learning? The problem is to devise a generalized approach for using physics information when learning or improving environment or system models, rather than methods that work only for one task or one environment.

evidence.quote: The concept of physics-informed RL involves incorporating physics structures, priors, and real-world physical variables into the policy learning or optimization process.

There has been a lot of research for better system identification or model learning through physics incorporation. But most works do not generalize well to different tasks and environments. To summarize, future works should address these crucial research goals: 1) model agnostic safe exploration and control using RL agents in complex and uncertain environments and 2) devise generalized approach of incorporating physics in data-driven Model learning.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a reinforcement learning setting in which an agent interacts with an environment whose dynamics are governed (at least in part) by known physical laws, expressible as differential equations, conservation laws, symmetries, or other structural priors. Let $\mathcal{T} = \{T_i\}$ denote a family of tasks (each specified by a reward function and possibly a time horizon) and let $\mathcal{E} = \{E_j\}$ denote a family of environments (each specified by a Markov decision process whose transition kernel obeys a common underlying class of physical constraints but may differ in parameters, geometry, or boundary conditions).

A physics-informed model learner is a procedure $\mathcal{L}$ that, given interaction data from one or more $(T_i, E_j)$ pairs together with physical priors $\Phi$ (e.g., PDE residuals, Lagrangian/Hamiltonian structure, invariances), produces an approximate dynamics model $\hat{f}_{\mathcal{L},\Phi}$ to be used for planning or policy optimization.

Problem: Devise a general-purpose construction $\mathcal{L}$ for incorporating the physical priors $\Phi$ into data-driven model learning such that the resulting model $\hat{f}_{\mathcal{L},\Phi}$ achieves provable or empirically demonstrable generalization across the full families $\mathcal{T}$ and $\mathcal{E}$ — that is, the same learning procedure, without task- or environment-specific re-engineering of how physics is injected, yields models whose prediction error and downstream control performance remain bounded uniformly (or with quantifiable degradation) over all $(T_i, E_j) \in \mathcal{T} \times \mathcal{E}$. Formally characterize such a procedure, identify sufficient conditions on $\Phi$, $\mathcal{T}$, and $\mathcal{E}$ under which it exists, and provide guarantees on its cross-task / cross-environment generalization.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a future research direction in surveys on physics-informed reinforcement learning, where most existing methods incorporate physics in task- or environment-specific ways and no generally accepted framework with cross-task / cross-environment generalization guarantees has been established.
